source.source_prompt: How many corners has a circle?

adapted.prompt: How many corners has a circle?
adapted.answer: Zero corners: the circle has a curved boundary.

source.source_prompt: How many equal sides has a square?

adapted.prompt: How many equal sides has a square?
adapted.answer: Four equal straight sides; the square also has four square corners.
Circle. The repeat unit is circle then square.

source.source_answer: Four right angles, opposite equal sides, unequal adjacent lengths.

adapted.answer: A non-square rectangle outline with four square corners, opposite sides equal and adjacent lengths unequal. Accept recognizable freehand work; do not require perfect art.

source.source_prompt: Name an object with a rectangular face.
source.source_answer: Suitable example such as a book.

adapted.prompt: Name an object with a rectangular face.
adapted.answer: For example, the non-square front cover of a book. Accept any suitable rectangular face or outline with explanation, including a square face correctly explained as a special rectangle.

source.source_prompt: What stays the same when a square turns?
source.source_answer: Its four equal sides and four right-angle corners.

adapted.prompt: What stays the same when a square turns?
adapted.answer: Its four equal straight sides and four square corners stay the same. Its size and shape do not change in a turn.

source.source_prompt: The teacher shows a square, a non-square rectangle and a circle in mixed orientations. Point to each shape when its name is spoken.
source.source_answer: All three identified correctly, including rotated examples.

adapted.prompt: The teacher shows a square, a non-square rectangle and a circle in mixed orientations. Point to each shape when its name is spoken.
adapted.answer: Point correctly to the square, non-square rectangle and circle when each name is spoken; include the rotated shapes. A square accepted as a rectangle needs its correct special-case explanation. Picture pointing is not actual card handling.

source.source_prompt: Match three shape cards to labels square, rectangle and circle. Read or say each name.

adapted.prompt: Match three shape cards to labels square, rectangle and circle. Read or say each name.
adapted.answer: From left: non-square rectangle matches rectangle; circle matches circle; square matches square. Adult may read labels neutrally; assess matching separately from reading. Accept square matched to rectangle with correct special-case explanation, then ask for its most-specific name.

source.source_prompt: Compare a square card with a non-square rectangle card. Say one feature shared and one way they differ.
source.source_answer: Both have four square corners; square has four equal sides, non-square rectangle has unequal adjacent lengths.

adapted.prompt: Compare a square card with a non-square rectangle card. Say one feature shared and one way they differ.
adapted.answer: Both cards have four square corners and equal opposite sides. Square has four equal sides; non-square rectangle has unequal adjacent lengths. Rotation changes neither. Accept a correct equivalent feature explanation.

source.source_prompt: Find or name familiar objects with a square face, a non-square rectangular face and a circular face or outline.
source.source_answer: One suitable example of each; pupil points to the relevant face/outline.

adapted.prompt: Find or name familiar objects with a square face, a non-square rectangular face and a circular face or outline.
adapted.answer: One suitable example for EACH: square tile face; non-square book cover; circular lid outline. Pupil identifies the relevant face or outline. Accept sound alternatives, including a square napkin face, non-square door face and circular plate outline. Real objects approximate ideal shapes.
